subject: general
question: Which of the following important Indian festivals was observed on 13th and 14th March 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Holi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Holi**, also known as the **Festival of Colours**, is a prominent Hindu festival celebrated with great fervor across India and in many parts of the world.
 
• It is observed on the **full moon day** of the Hindu month of **Phalguna**, which typically falls in March. In 2025, Holi was celebrated on **13th and 14th March**.
 
• Holi signifies the victory of **good over evil**, marking the triumph of Lord Vishnu's devotee **Prahlada** over the demoness **Holika**. Hence, it is a culturally significant event.
 
• The festival is celebrated with various traditions such as **Holika Dahan** (bonfire on the eve of Holi) and the playful throwing of **colored powders** and water on each other.
 
• Holi serves as an occasion for people to come together, bury past grievances, and strengthen social bonds. *Hence, the correct answer is Holi.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Celebration of Holi:**

 
 
• Holi is celebrated in two main phases: **Holika Dahan** and **Rangwali Holi**. Holika Dahan involves lighting a bonfire to symbolize the defeat of evil forces, while Rangwali Holi is marked by the playful throwing of colored powders and water.
 
• People sing, dance, and enjoy festive food such as **gujiya**, **thandai**, and other traditional sweets during the celebrations.
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance:**
 
 
• Holi is rooted in Hindu mythology, particularly the story of **Prahlada** and **Holika**. Prahlada's unwavering devotion to Lord Vishnu and his survival from the fire set by Holika is celebrated as a victory of faith and goodness.
 
• **Lord Krishna** and his playful use of colors with Radha and the gopis is also associated with the festival, adding a romantic and joyous dimension to Holi.
 
 
 
• **Regional Variations:**
 
 
• While Holi is celebrated throughout India, the traditions differ from region to region. For example, in **Vrindavan** and **Barsana**, Lathmar Holi involves women playfully hitting men with sticks.
 
• In **Bengal**, Holi is celebrated as **Dol Jatra**, focusing on devotion to Lord Krishna and Radha.
 
 
 
• **Global Celebrations:**
 
 
• Holi has become popular in many countries outside India, including the **United States**, **United Kingdom**, and **Australia**, as a celebration of joy, unity, and diversity.
 
• Events such as the **"Festival of Colors"** organized in various parts of the world attract participants from diverse cultures and ethnicities.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of Holika Dahan:**

 
 
• Holika Dahan is performed on the eve of Holi to signify the burning of evil forces. People gather around the bonfire, chant prayers, and seek blessings for prosperity and health.
 
• The bonfire is often made with wood and dried leaves, symbolizing the end of the cold season and the arrival of spring.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Concerns:**
 
 
• In recent years, awareness has been raised about the environmental impact of Holi celebrations, such as the excessive use of water and harmful chemical colors.
 
• Eco-friendly practices, like using natural or organic colors and conserving water, have been promoted to make the festival more sustainable.
